newsitem.title: UK: UK buyouts hit 3.9 billion stg in first half.
newsitem.headline: UK buyouts hit 3.9 billion stg in first half.

text.p: The UK buyout market set a rapid pace in the first half, with 298 deals worth 3.9 billion stg completed, according to a new survey.

Buyout activity is at "exceptional levels," said a survey by the Centre for Management Buy-Out Research (CMBOR) at Nottingham University, though the market failed to keep pace with the record 4.5 billion stg in deals booked in the first half of 1996.
The fall-off can partly be attributed to a slowdown in buyouts after the general election, with many deals shelved until the details of next Wednesday's budget are known, according to CMBOR.

"With a favourable budget, specifically in terms of limited tax increases or other majors changes, and assuming no significant interest rate rises, we anticipate notable UK activity in the next six months," said Stephan Welton, senior director of BZW Private Equity.
An increasingly competitive and expensive market for buyouts in the UK has led to more innovative financing of deals and an increased focus on Continental buyouts, according to CMBOR.

The focus on Europe is expected to continue, as evinced by more than 1.5 billion stg of new Europe-oriented private equity funds that have been launched in recent months, notably a $1 billion fund from Schroders Ventures and a 800 million stg fund launched by Charterhouse Development Capital.

"Great liquidity in the market is giving rise to a funnelling of funds from venture houses into Europe and the appearance of several mega-deals, such as the Mettler-Toledo and Geberit transactions in Switzerland, which interestingly have also seen the emergence in the use of the junk bond as part of the financing package," according to CMBOR.
London and south east England have reversed a negative trend and seen 100 deals completed in the period.
CMBOR was founded by Deloitte & Touche Corporate Finance and BZW Private Equity. -- James Saft, London newsroom +171 542 2734
